text.p: American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) in Mexican media conglomerate Grupo Televisa fell on Thursday amid a slide in the Mexico City exchange.
ADRs were mixed as foreign markets shook off warnings by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan that stocks were overvalued.
"They are generally better. Most markets have shrugged off Greenspan's comments," a trader said.
Televisa was off 7/8 to 25 in heavy volume. The ADRs were among the most active shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

A trader said Televisa had been weighed by lingering concerns about the health of the company's chairman. Televisa has said the executive, Emilio Azcarraga, would give up some of his duties after undergoing medical tests this month.

The company also was hit by a slide in Mexico on profit-taking, worries about Greenspan's comments and the possibility of an increase in domestic interest rates. Televisa reported late on Wednesday advance advertising deposits for 1997 were up almost 10 percent over last year.
Among other Latin American ADRs, Brazilian telephone holding Telebras was unchanged at 97-7/8 after it reported 1996 income in line with expectations.
Gucci rose two to 65-1/4 in moderate volume ahead of the release of its 1996 earnings.
Among Asian ADRs, China's Jilin Chemical Industrial Co was up 5/8 to 14-1/8 and South Korea's Korea Electric Power Corp fell 3/4 to 17-7/8.
Decliners barely led advancers by a margin of 248 to 240 among 807 ADRs. Volume was 38 million shares at midday.
